fact: UNESCO reports that regulators and policymakers from Guinea-Bissau, with Angola, Sao Tome and Principe and Mozambique (more than 40 in all), took part in a data governance workshop in Maputo on 8-10 December 2025, organised by UNESCO with Mozambique's INTIC and Smart Africa; attendance only, no agreement signed.

AUDA-NEPAD, the African Union's development agency, launched on 24 July 2026 at the STC-TTIM ministerial segment in Abidjan its Programme for African Developing Island Economies, which Guinea-Bissau joins with six other island states; digital transformation is one of its six pillars, and the programme runs on a 2026-2031 roadmap.
